verdict.rationale: Auth0 documents securing APIs with OAuth 2.0 using scopes and granular permissions. Its AI marketing explicitly claims agents get identities for more secure access to MCP servers, so an MCP server could plausibly sit behind Auth0-issued scoped tokens. However, no evidence shows MCP-authorization-spec compliance or a documented guide for protecting a remote MCP server. The Auth0 MCP Server is a tenant-management tool, not a way to protect your own server, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: documented MCP-spec-compliant authorization flow (e.g. dynamic client registration, protected-resource metadata), an MCP-server protection guide, and hands-on or independent corroboration.
